one_liner: Licensed mental health counselor who directs a VA Vet Center, supervising clinicians, running outreach and budgets, and providing readjustment counseling to veterans.
fit_summary: This GS-13 job has hard basic requirements: a CACREP-accredited master's or doctorate in clinical mental health counseling, plus a full, unrestricted license to practice independently as an LPMHC. Nothing on file shows Daniel has either. Daniel's emergency-management consulting, policy knowledge, and outreach skills match only the administrative and Congressional-liaison parts of the role, so you would not qualify as things stand.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens), but must meet Title 38 basic requirements; this is not a status-only posting.
Master's or doctoral degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling or a related field from a CACREP-accredited program, with a transcript submitted with the application.
Full, current, unrestricted license to independently practice as a Licensed Professional Mental Health Counselor, including diagnosis and treatment.
At least one year of progressively complex experience equivalent to GS-12, showing advanced clinical practice skills and judgment.
Background investigation, seasonal flu vaccination requirement, REAL ID-compliant identification, and a 1- or 2-year trial period.
strategy: Do not apply unless you hold a CACREP-accredited clinical counseling degree and an independent LPMHC license. Without both, HR will rate you ineligible no matter how strong your resume is.

Instead, search USAJOBS for Title 5 Vet Center roles open to the public, such as Outreach Specialist (often GS-0101) or Program Support Assistant, which use the same Vet Center outreach model without a clinical license.

Also target VA, FEMA, and HHS roles in congressional affairs or emergency management (GS-0301, GS-0089, GS-0343). There your IEM consulting and policy knowledge count directly toward specialized experience.

Frame your IEM work by the government clients served and the concrete tasks you did, such as preparedness planning, recovery program support, stakeholder briefings, or data reporting. Keep it to a few tight bullets that fit the two-page limit.
If a clinical VA career appeals long-term, research CACREP programs and Virginia LPC licensure, which requires supervised residency hours after the degree. Treat it as a multi-year path.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client type] [preparedness/recovery] programs at IEM by [specific task, e.g., coordinating stakeholder meetings], working with [number] agency partners; [hours/week], [dates].
Prepared briefings and reports on [topic] for [client/officials], translating policy and program data into recommendations used for [purpose].
Conducted community outreach to [population] during [event/program], building relationships with [partner organizations] to connect residents with [services].
interview_questions: Describe how you would plan outreach to veterans in rural or underserved parts of a service area.
Tell us about a time you briefed elected officials or their staff on a program.
How have you used data to monitor program outcomes and improve performance?
Describe how you managed competing priorities across multiple sites or teams.
watch_outs: Hard degree and license requirement: you cannot qualify without a CACREP clinical counseling degree and an independent LPMHC license.
Very short application window (October 28 to November 4, 2026), and a missing transcript disqualifies an application.
Not a remote job; it is on-site at a Vet Center with some nights and weekends, no relocation (PCS) pay, and no promotion potential beyond GS-13.
